paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Solomon says a good name is more desirable than great riches (Proverbs 22:1), and then he spends sixteen verses showing what a good name is made of. It's made of humility and the fear of the LORD, which bring "wealth and honor and life" (Proverbs 22:4). It's also made of a generous hand, a pure heart and gracious lips (Proverbs 22:9, 11).

Now look at the other side. The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences (Proverbs 22:3). The slacker has an excuse ready for everything, and the one who sows injustice reaps disaster (Proverbs 22:8, 13). I've been the simple one, friend, and the oven does NOT care how sure I felt. Every little choice is a seed, and the harvest shows up whether you're ready or not.

Here's what holds it all together: "The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all." (Proverbs 22:2). So nobody gets to be ground down to get ahead, and nobody gets to be bought off with a gift to the rich (Proverbs 22:16). And when you train a child in the way he should go (Proverbs 22:6), you're handing down that same wisdom. So baker, build a name worth more than silver and gold, and let the LORD who made everyone be the One you listen to.
